QUESTION 1 — Of the 8 supplied HPO terms, how many does MVA1 explain?
==================================================================================
  MVA1 (OMIM:257300): 57 annotated terms, 244 after propagation

  🔴 A count of 'features explained' is worthless without grading it. HPO is a
  DAG, so EVERY term is reachable from any disease through a high-enough ancestor
  — 'All' sits at the root. What matters is how SPECIFIC the connecting term is,
  so each row reports the information content of the link that does the work.

  (term names are not shown; counts only)

  🔴 Link grades: 2 direct, 1 specific,
  2 generic, 3 vacuous.
  Only 3 of 8 terms are matched in a way that carries
  real information. An earlier draft of this script reported '8 of 8 explained',
  which was true and meaningless — a very general term was being
  'explained' by the root term 'All'.

VERDICT
==================================================================================
  MVA1 ranks 3 of 12,867 diseases sharing any feature (top 0.0%),
  and matches 3 of the 8 supplied HPO terms informatively
  (2 direct, 1 via a specific ancestor).

  🔴 Phenotype similarity places MVA1 among the top diseases without singling it out;
  this script shows compatibility, and the genotype identifies the gene.

  What it establishes is narrower and still worth having:
    • MVA1 is phenotypically COMPATIBLE with the supplied terms, not contradicted.
    • No disease ranking above it is one whose gene the child also carries a
      rare damaging biallelic genotype in — which is the conjunction that
      actually identifies the answer.

  The genotype does the identifying. The phenotype does the not-ruling-out.
  Stating which is which is the point of running this in the reverse direction.
